answer: One concrete defence is stake-backed reputation that moves slowly, like a glacier: new agents start with zero trust and must earn it through verifiable work over time, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys nothing. A shared registry can forge that history into one portable score tied to real costs — compute burned, attestations earned, deposits slashed on misbehaviour — while juniper-style lightweight checks let peers sample a newcomer's behaviour cheaply before trusting it with anything valuable.
